system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and reviewer note have no contractual effect and should be disregarded. The package materially shifts known and unknown pre-Completion risk to the Buyer.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% of price / AUD 4.8m**. | A cap of **50% / AUD 12m**, with no cap applying to excluded claim categories; any lower fallback should depend on diligence and insurance. | **Reject 20% and propose 50%.** — With no identified W&I protection, AUD 4.8m provides inadequate recourse for a AUD 24m acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 deductible basket, so only excess is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, aggregation of related matters, and a **tipping basket**: propose AUD 10,000 per claim and AUD 100,000 aggregate. | **Counter with AUD 10,000/AUD 100,000 and first-dollar recovery once the basket is met.** — The proposed deductible basket leaves the Buyer bearing a material layer of valid loss. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | General Warranty Claims expire 18 months after Completion; Seller seeks to apply limitation periods to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months**, preferably 36 months, with timely notice preserving the claim even if quantum is not yet final. | **Require 24 months minimum and confine it to general Warranty Claims.** — Eighteen months may not cover two full reporting and audit cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap, thresholds and 18-month period as general warranties. | Capacity, authority and title claims capped at **100% of the price**, with no thresholds and a six-year period; title should preferably survive without contractual time bar. | **Create a separate fundamental warranty regime: 100% cap, no basket/de minimis, six years or longer for title.** — The Buyer must have full recourse if it does not acquire the shares and ownership promised. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | No express carve-out; “all Claims of any nature” are subject to caps, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions. | Express preservation of claims for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct and deliberate concealment, including relevant conduct by the Seller’s transaction personnel. | **Add an overriding fraud/dishonesty carve-out from every limitation and exclusive-remedy provision.** — The Seller must not obtain contractual protection for intentionally dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | Purports to disclose the entire data room, Accounts, registers and all publicly searchable corporate records, including anything “contained or referred to” there. | Only matters **fairly and specifically disclosed**, against identified warranties, in sufficient detail to understand their nature and likely effect; no constructive public-record disclosure. | **Delete general disclosure and require specific, warranty-linked disclosure in the Disclosure Letter.** — A data dump does not give the Buyer sufficiently clear notice of exceptions to the warranties. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for matters known by the Buyer or advisers, including matters discoverable from the data room or public records. | Preferably no knowledge exclusion; failing that, only actual knowledge of a short list of named senior Buyer deal-team members, without enquiry, imputation or adviser knowledge. | **Delete constructive and adviser knowledge and limit any qualifier to actual knowledge of named individuals.** — “Discoverable” information would convert incomplete diligence into a broad waiver of contractual protection. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller uses reasonable endeavours; condition is treated as satisfied upon delivery of written consent, although the consent and satisfaction of its conditions are absent. | A genuine Buyer-controlled CP requiring unconditional written consent/waiver, satisfaction of all conditions, and no fee, amendment or adverse term without Buyer approval. | **Do not complete until compliant Bluefen consent is delivered in form and substance satisfactory to Buyer.** — Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue, making conditional or adverse consent unacceptable. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; release is to be provided after Completion. | Exact payout statement, direct repayment through funds flow, and effective release at or before Completion of all security, guarantees and claims, with only ministerial registrations permitted afterward. | **Make repayment and effective discharge simultaneous Completion deliverables.** — The Buyer should not acquire the Company subject to Seller-era debt or security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 of Completion bonuses are said to be for the Seller but are omitted from funds flow; payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs are unresolved. | Treat the bonuses and all applicable on-costs as Seller transaction expenses, paid by the Seller or deducted dollar-for-dollar from price and fully provided for in funds flow. | **Add the gross bonuses and all verified on-costs to Completion deductions or Seller-funded payments.** — Completion-triggered transaction costs must not reduce the Buyer’s debt-free/cash-free value after closing. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity is limited to the specific SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 remains open and there is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Pre-Completion payment and written confirmation of transfer, plus a separate indemnity covering all loss from non-payment, defective chain of title, infringement or inability to use the Project Materials. | **Require payment and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables and broaden the indemnity outside general limitations.** — Reimbursing a fee alone does not cure loss of ownership or use of material IP. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope and notification obligations remain unknown. | A completed forensic investigation, preservation and remediation evidence, legal assessment of notification duties, ongoing cooperation, and a specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require satisfactory investigation/remediation before Completion and a specific indemnity with regulatory-period survival.** — Unknown access to approximately 1,240 records creates unquantified regulatory, remediation and reputational exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals—AUD 330,000 total—are characterised as ordinary-course operating costs despite uncertainty over timing, scope and termination. | Full contracts and invoices, confirmation of term and termination rights, no renewal or variation without Buyer consent, and proper allocation of pre-Completion or non-ordinary liabilities. | **Investigate and reflect any pre-Completion, accrued or non-ordinary amount in the price/funds flow, with Seller indemnity if necessary.** — The present disclosure does not establish that the Buyer receives corresponding post-Completion value. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply caps, thresholds, time limits, non-reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | A clear claims taxonomy: general warranties only under the general regime; separate treatment for fundamental warranties, tax covenant, specific indemnities, debt, leakage, price adjustment, Completion obligations and fraud. | **Rewrite the limitations clause to state exhaustively which provisions apply to each claim category.** — An “all Claims” formulation could neutralise specifically negotiated protection and payment obligations. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies solely on the Company’s share register at DD-012 as evidence that the Seller owns 100% of the shares. | Corroborating constitutional, corporate and transactional records, share certificates, transfer/allotment history, ASIC and security searches, confirmation of beneficial ownership and absence of encumbrances, plus valid transfers at Completion. | **Make satisfactory title verification and clean transfer documents a Completion requirement.** — A company-maintained register is important evidence but does not alone eliminate competing ownership, beneficial interest or security risks. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are “settled” under the general 20%/18-month regime. | Separate tax covenant and warranties surviving the relevant statutory period plus a buffer, normally up to a 100% cap; enhanced core-IP ownership warranties and specific treatment of Ironquay. | **Reopen and separately negotiate tax and IP: tax survival of seven years or statutory period plus six months, and enhanced recourse for core-IP ownership.** — Tax liabilities emerge late, while ownership of core analytics IP is fundamental to the acquired business’s value. |

**Priority completion blockers:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark repayment and release, Ironquay payment/assignment, resolution of the bonus funds flow, and satisfactory investigation of the export/privacy incident. The Buyer should also reject any updated disclosure that unilaterally qualifies warranties after signing or cures a failed condition without its written consent.
=== END ADVICE ===
